**No issue found.** I left the target source unchanged at generator SHA-256 `b81daf3ec87cf80d6748ed2220885a57fc0baef944eafb5fab0247994b096a2a` and rule hash `259314225434`.

I checked the complete 12-stage battery, all 21 task-local tests, exact-axis behavior, validator strength, live-Racket parity, and the retained source-bound lesson probe. The battery is 12/12 green at `checks/audit/b35816e8388b-battery/checks/b35816e8388b_before_battery_summary.json`; focused tests are 21/21 at `checks/audit/b35816e8388b/task-tests.log`. The probe assembled 120 lessons per band (360 total, 1,440 generated examples) using three consecutive demonstrations plus the next query. It found 120/120 identifiable lessons in each band, 352/480, 374/480, and 388/480 unique inputs for easy/medium/hard, and zero complete demonstration sets survived for any declared competitor; see `checks/audit/b35816e8388b/lesson-probe.json`.

The most plausible canonical shortcut is “always paint the fixed grid center.” It fits both canonical training pairs, but the generator’s deterministic off-center profile refuted it on 434/480 easy, 436/480 medium, and 454/480 hard examples in the probe. I also considered bounding-box center, arithmetic coordinate mean, orientation-specific midpoint, keeping endpoints, and painting the full segment. The first two are equivalent to the intended rule on the lawful even-span domain; the others are directly refuted. This is finite rival testing, not proof against every possible induction.
